name: Golden Ticket Attack (Rubeus / SafetyKatz)
description: Forge a TGT (Golden Ticket) using the krbtgt NTLM hash. Grants persistent access to all domain Kerberos services with arbitrary user impersonation.

recommended.note: Use golden ticket for cross-domain escalation

notes: Default lifetime 10 years. Reset krbtgt password TWICE to invalidate all golden tickets. Detectable by ticket anomalies (10yr lifetime, missing PAC validation).

defense.why_it_works: The krbtgt account's NTLM hash is the key material used to sign all Kerberos TGTs in a domain. Possessing the krbtgt hash allows forging arbitrary TGTs (Golden Tickets) for any user, with any group memberships, valid for any time period. Rubeus /golden or Mimikatz kerberos::golden creates the forged ticket locally — no DC interaction needed. The forged ticket is accepted by any Kerberos service in the domain.
defense.prerequisites: krbtgt NTLM hash (from DCSync or NTDS.dit dump). Domain SID. Target username and RID to forge. Rubeus or Mimikatz. Any host with network access to domain services.
defense.impact: T1558.001 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Golden Ticket. Indefinite domain persistence — the forged TGT is valid until the krbtgt password is rotated twice. Allows impersonating any user including DA, accessing any domain service. Survives DA password resets; only double-rotation of krbtgt removes access.
defense.detection:
Event 4769 (TGS request) with a TGT that has anomalous properties: ticket lifetime > 10 hours, non-standard encryption, or group SIDs that don't match the claimed username. MDI: 'Golden Ticket usage' alert — detects when ticket attributes don't match the account's real properties in AD. Event 4768 missing before 4769 (Golden Ticket skips AS-REQ). Forged tickets from Mimikatz often have default 10-year lifetime.
Anomalous Kerberos activity: forged or stolen tickets by correlating malformed fields in logon events, RC4-encrypted TGTs, or TGS requests without corresponding TGT requests; suspicious processes accessing LSASS memory for ticket extraction (DET0522/AN1443).
Suspicious access to SSSD secrets database and Kerberos key material indicating ticket theft or replay; correlate anomalous file access with unusual Kerberos service ticket requests (AN1444).
Forging or replaying Kerberos tickets: monitor Unified Logs for anomalous kinit/klist activity and unusual authentication sequences (AN1445).
defense.artifacts: MDI alert: 'Golden Ticket usage detected' | Event 4769 with anomalous ticket lifetime or missing prior 4768 | Kerberos authentication from unexpected host for DA account | SIEM: Event 4769 with PAC claiming DA membership for non-DA account
defense.prevention:
Double-rotate the krbtgt password immediately after any suspected compromise (two rotations required — old hash cached on DCs). Use 'Protected Users' group for DA accounts (doesn't prevent Golden Ticket if krbtgt hash is known, but reduces exposure surface). MDI deployment — best detection. Restrict DA logon to PAWs. Implement tiering to limit blast radius even with a Golden Ticket.
Active Directory Configuration: Reset KRBTGT account password twice (invalidates all golden tickets); rotate every 180 days.
Audit: Scan for insecure Kerberos configurations.
Credential Access Protection: On Linux, use SELinux to protect Kerberos key material.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Enable AES Kerberos encryption instead of RC4.
Password Policies: Service accounts should have 25+ character passwords; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA).
Privileged Account Management: Limit domain admin to DCs only; restrict service account privileges.
defense.evasion: Set realistic ticket lifetime (10 hours) to match normal TGT defaults. Use current encryption type (AES256 instead of RC4). Set the forged PAC to match what the real account would have, avoid adding extra SIDs. Request tickets shortly before use to avoid stale-ticket detection.
defense.misconfiguration: krbtgt password never rotated (common — default AD never rotates krbtgt). Default ticket lifetime settings allow 10-hour TGTs. MDI not deployed. No detection of PAC anomalies in ticketing events.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# krbtgt password age (should be < 6 months):
Get-ADUser krbtgt -Properties PasswordLastSet | Select-Object PasswordLastSet
# PasswordLastSet: 2018-01-01 — 6+ years old = krbtgt hash stable for years
# If attacker got hash, they have indefinite Golden Ticket capability

# Default ticket lifetime (10 hours) matches attacker-forged defaults:
# Computer Config → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Account Policies → Kerberos Policy
# Maximum lifetime for user ticket: 10 hours (matches Mimikatz default)
defense.secure_config:
# Rotate krbtgt password TWICE (to invalidate all existing Golden Tickets):
# Run 24 hours apart (to allow DC replication between rotations):
$newpw = (New-Object System.Security.SecureString)
# Or use the Microsoft KRBTGT_UpdateResetKrbtgtAccount tool:
# https://github.com/microsoft/New-KrbtgtKeys.ps1
.\New-KrbtgtKeys.ps1 -Mode EnableAES
# Run again 10+ hours later for second rotation

# MDI: deploy sensors on all DCs — Golden Ticket detection is built-in
# Alert triggers when ticket attributes don't match AD account properties

# Restrict DA account logon via Authentication Policy Silos:
New-ADAuthenticationPolicySilo -Name 'DA-Silo'
New-ADAuthenticationPolicy -Name 'DA-PAW-Policy' -UserAllowedToAuthenticateFrom 'PAW-Computers-SG'
Get-ADGroupMember 'Domain Admins' | ForEach-Object { Set-ADUser $_ -AuthenticationPolicySilo 'DA-Silo' }
